record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.context_brief: Borel complexity inside a full group
record.original_question: For a fixed ergodic transformation T0 with full group [T0], is the conjugacy relation on [T0] Borel? If not, does it become Borel after restricting to ergodic transformations?

evidence.quote: Let us first fix an ergodic transformation T0, and define its full group [T0] as the group of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X such that for all x, the point U(x) belongs to the T0-orbit of x.
Question 4.5. Is the conjugacy relation on [T0] Borel? If no, is it when restricted to ergodic transformations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving bimeasurable bijections of $(X,\mu)$, identified modulo equality almost everywhere. Fix an ergodic transformation $T_0 \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$, and define its full group
$$[T_0] = \{U \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu) : U(x) \text{ belongs to the } T_0\text{-orbit of } x \text{ for almost every } x \in X\}.$$
Equip $[T_0]$ with the uniform metric $d_u(U,V) = \mu(\{x : U(x) \ne V(x)\})$, with respect to which $[T_0]$ is a Polish group. Consider the conjugacy equivalence relation on $[T_0]$, namely
$$U \sim V \iff \exists S \in [T_0]\ \text{such that}\ V = S U S^{-1}.$$

(a) Is $\sim$ a Borel subset of $[T_0] \times [T_0]$?

(b) If not, is the restriction of $\sim$ to the set of ergodic elements of $[T_0]$ a Borel equivalence relation?
artifact.category_tag: Borel complexity of conjugacy in full groups
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (October 2025) shows that the isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel reducible to the conjugacy relation induced by the action of a full group [T0] on itself, and that this relation is "unbalanced." This addresses related questions of Le Maître but does not directly determine whether the conjugacy relation on [T0] (or its restriction to ergodic elements) is Borel. No definitive resolution of the Borelness question was located.

status_evidence.title: Unbalancedness of the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations
status_evidence.snippet: The isomorphism of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel reducible to the relation induced by the conjugacy action of the full group of an ergodic measure-preserving transformation on itself.
status_evidence.claim: Recent paper addresses related questions of Le Maître about the conjugacy action on full groups but does not directly resolve whether the conjugacy relation on [T0] is Borel.

status_evidence.title: The conjugacy problem in ergodic theory
status_evidence.snippet: The conjugacy relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of (X,μ) is a complete analytic set, hence not Borel.
status_evidence.claim: Classical conjugacy on all of Aut(X,μ) restricted to ergodic transformations is known to be complete analytic, but this is a different ambient setting than within a fixed full group [T0].
